ns2:section.sectionText: This course will examine different approaches to the nature of knowledge of the external world; arguments for and against the existence of God; the possibility of free will; and central issues in theoretical and applied ethics, including the grounds of right action, our relationship with the environment, and the meaning of life. Themes in existential philosophy ? such as a focus on action over thought, freedom, responsibility, suffering, absurdity, nothingness, and so on ? will figure prominently throughout. Students will be required to take reading quizzes, participate in class, write two short papers, and take a midterm and final exam.
